record_body:
Account summary
- Product: Cascade is a customer-support platform building an AI agent + agent-assist experiences (chat + retrieval over KB + internal tickets).
- Current state: live on Redwood Hosted API for chat + embeddings; evaluating Dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation as enterprise usage grows.
- Reference program fit: good for reference calls (peer-to-peer), lower likelihood of public case study (legal + brand constraints). CS recommends “private reference” positioning.

Key contacts / relationship notes
- Champion (product/eng): Head of AI (prefers to stay off-record; okay with 1:1 reference calls if scoped tightly).
- Exec sponsor: VP Support Ops interested in credibility with enterprise buyers but cautious about any public statements.
- CS relationship: generally positive; they value fast incident response + guidance on batching/caching. Sensitive to being ‘oversubscribed’ for calls.
- Quote from CS check-in: “We can talk about architecture + what we learned, but please don’t ask us to publish numbers or name vendor comparisons.”

Use case & requirements (current + expansion)
- Workloads
  - Agent assist chat: streaming responses in the agent console.
  - Customer-facing bot: lower token budget, strict guardrails.
  - Embeddings: ticket/KB ingestion + nightly refresh; intermittent spikes during bulk re-index.
  - Reranking: exploring for improved retrieval quality.
- Performance targets (internal / not for publication)
  - Interactive chat: p95 latency goal under ~1.5–2.0s for typical short responses (streaming acceptable).
  - High variance traffic; predictable capacity during weekday business hours.
- Cost sensitivity: medium-high. They actively tune prompts and want clear levers (batching/caching) + visibility into cost per conversation.
- Model preferences: open model options acceptable; wants ability to pin versions + rollback quickly to avoid regressions.
- Routing/fallback needs: interested in policy-based fallback during incident windows (keep app online, degrade gracefully).

Security / compliance
- SOC2 required for vendor review; SSO/SAML expected for Console.
- Audit logging requested for enterprise workflows (who accessed what, admin actions). Retention controls needed for logs.
- Data handling: does not require on-prem/air-gap; prefers US regions; asks for clarity on data retention for prompts/completions.

Reference readiness (internal)
- Willingness:
  - Reference calls: conditional yes.
  - Public case study / logo: likely no (at least until 2026; needs legal sign-off + comms approval).
- Topics they are comfortable discussing on calls:
  - Why they chose Redwood (developer experience, stability, operational controls).
  - How they integrated chat + embeddings quickly (time-to-value).
  - How they think about fallbacks, evaluation, and rollout safety.
- Topics to avoid:
  - Exact $/token or vendor price comparisons.
  - Exact latency numbers; can talk in qualitative terms (“material improvement”, “more consistent p95”).
  - Any customer names in their own platform.

Recent activity timeline (high level)
- 2025-08: Expansion conversation opened (Dedicated capacity sizing; expected Q4).
- 2025-09: Reliability concerns raised after a brief performance incident; recovered quickly but left “public claims” sensitivity.
- 2025-10-15: Internal CS guardrails circulated (limit reference load; log outcomes back to HubSpot).
- 2025-10-22: CS-led sync on reference-call playbook + prep (Fireflies: 2025-10-22-cascade-customer-support-reference-call-playbook-sync).

Procurement / deal notes
- Buying motion: enterprise procurement driven by their largest customer deal; wants Dedicated quote + SLA language.
- Timeline: aiming to complete vendor review + pricing approval by 2025-12 if security questionnaires can be completed quickly.

Next steps (owner + CS)
- Avery: send Dedicated pricing ranges + proposed SLA options; confirm whether reference calls can begin pre-contract (CS recommends yes, but with tight scope).
- Rachel (CS): propose a reference-call cadence policy (max 1/month, 10 business days lead time, opt-out at any time, pre-brief required).
- Markus (SE): provide a short, non-confidential architecture overview they can use on calls (no metrics; focus on patterns: batching/caching, fallback policy, version pinning).

Internal tags
- Reference type: “Private reference calls (scoped)”
- Risk: “Public story not likely in 2025; revisit post-expansion + after 2–3 stable quarters”
